method: Engine self-test executed at tested_commit via py3.11 (HL_Live_Copy_Service_Core.py --self-test, exit 0, 145 checks, RESULT::CLEAN_LIVE_COPY_CORE_SELF_TEST_PASS), plus an importable-module severity/terminal-state probe and targeted reads of _archive/hl_stage2/HL_Live_Copy_Service_Core.py and HL_Copy_App_SSOT.py at the same commit.

rows.evidence_ref: Core.py CopyAccountIngestor.copy_fill_id; self-test 103-109 and 115-120; grep -i untrusted Core.py+SSOT.py = 0 hits
rows.why: Dedupe on exchange hash:tid/oid works and duplicate/replay is audit-only, but when hash/tid are absent the key is a synthesised stable_hash over coin/side/px/sz/time/intent_id and no 'untrusted' marking exists anywhere (0 hits), so the absent/ambiguous case is silently trusted - the half of the row that forbids it is missing.

rows.evidence_ref: Core.py _reduce_only_for_intent L3199-3206 and close_size L2945; self-test 133-134, 138 (EXIT wire reduce_only=True), 139 (ENTRY False), 141 (one close per burst), 144 (ledger short stays -2598.0)
rows.why: Row-bound to reductions: the EXIT wire payload carries reduce_only=True while ENTRY carries False, so the exchange caps the close at actual account-net and cannot flip through flat, and check 144 proves a close burst never flips the ledger short; an entry-side change would fail these checks.

rows.evidence_ref: Core.py pre-exchange Gate B (min notional applies to ENTRY/ADD/EXIT; terminal_state DUST_BELOW_MIN_NOTIONAL, exchange_called False); probe classify_operator_action -> HOLD_DUST_OR_AGGREGATE, classify_integrity_severity -> AMBER
rows.why: The sub-min close is detected before any send call, exchange_called is False so nothing is transmitted, and the outcome is a telemetry block (AMBER / HOLD_DUST_OR_AGGREGATE) - one of the sanctioned dispositions; a different row would not produce this terminal state or operator action.

rows.evidence_ref: Self-test 38, 40 (wallet A exit clamped to sleeve 5.0 while coin_net=2.0), 72, 87; Core.py close_size L2945
rows.why: Four checks assert the opposite of the row: exit size is deliberately clamped to the per-wallet sleeve, not to the single account-level coin net (sleeve 5 vs coin_net 2 sizes 5), so sleeves do size orders and the account-level-target requirement is genuinely unmet.

rows.evidence_ref: Core.py run_cycle Gate 1 (blocks only when HL_LIVE_WS_ENABLED and worst_health_grade DEGRADED); WSManager.write_health L4932-4980; self-test 1 (WS_DISABLED, wallets LIVE, leader_intents_written=1)
rows.why: No per-wallet block on unproven subscription: with WS_DISABLED wallets are LIVE and intents are written, the WS env flag defaults off so Gate 1 is inert, and staleness is folded into one global grade that blocks all wallets at once rather than the stale wallet.

rows.evidence_ref: Core.py ExchangeReconciler.compare_snapshot L5866-5892 and fetch_snapshot L5668-5684 (live clearinghouseState -> positions_by_coin); self-test 28-29 and 30 (manual-only ZEC exposure reported MISMATCH, action ASSIGN_OR_REPAIR_PROVEN_POSITION)
rows.why: The target is a live exchange read compared against the engine ledger net, not two local artifacts agreeing; check 30 is row-bound proof that a ledger-only position with zero exchange position is a reported books mismatch and cannot be green.

rows.evidence_ref: Core.py entry gates L6350-6362 (WS_FEED_STALE, COPY_POLL_STALE, UNRECONCILED_FILLED_SENDS, TOO_MANY_ACTIVE_WALLETS, daily loss); grep LEDGER_EXCHANGE_NET_MISMATCH -> only L5889/L5892 and self-tests
rows.why: exchange_recon_status is audited and summarised but consumed by no gate: a LEDGER_EXCHANGE_NET_MISMATCH never sets _entry_sends_blocked_reason and never forces close-only or halt (CLOSE_ONLY is only a per-wallet config mode), so unresolved desired-vs-actual mismatch leaves ENTRY/ADD enabled.

rows.evidence_ref: Self-test 1 (master gate off: leader_sends_attempted 0); Core.py L3261-3262 early return MASTER_REAL_ORDERS_OFF; grep enumerate Core.py -> only asset-universe loops L3930/L4025
rows.why: The behavioural half holds but the required gate TEST that enumerates every exchange-client call site does not exist - the only enumerate loops are asset universes and the guard is one early return, so a new call path bypassing L3261 would go undetected.

rows.evidence_ref: grep -i openOrders over Core.py+SSOT.py = 0 hits; grep -i refetch Core.py = 0 hits; only snapshot fetch is ExchangeReconciler.fetch_snapshot L5668 behind --reconcile-exchange L7977
rows.why: There is no open-orders read in the product and no per-event refetch of exchange actual after an order update, fill or reject - reconciliation is an optional cycle flag - so the precondition for the next order is absent, not merely untested.

rows.evidence_ref: grep -c truth_tier Core.py SSOT.py -> 0 / 0; grep -ci freshness Core.py SSOT.py -> 0 / 0
rows.why: Neither truth_tier nor freshness_age exists as a value attribute in the engine or SSOT layer, so no value can carry them and no stale/unavailable value can be programmatically or visually blocked on them.

rows.evidence_ref: Self-test 1-5 (gate dominance: zero send attempts, no live_positions.json); 28/29/80/81 (exchange actual vs ledger, no auto-correct); 31-37 (restart/cutover: live_start_ms stable, wiped state rebuilds); 103-120 (duplicate and cross-process replay of copy fill and OID blocked without double mutation)
rows.why: Each of the four named invariant families has an explicit, external assertion in the primary in-engine suite (exchange artefacts absent, exchange-vs-ledger comparison, state survival across restart, second identical event cannot move the ledger); a row outside these families could not satisfy them.

rows.evidence_ref: Core.py build_live_integrity_status L1037-1090+ (recomputed from persisted sends/fills/recon, restart cutoff, hard-copy counts); self-test 122-127 (safety-gate, ownership-gate, no-position close, EXIT_RECOVERY_QUEUED, SDK-unavailable close, manual recovery all classified)
rows.why: Health is a continuously recomputed account-level invariant over the audit CSVs plus the exchange snapshot with a restart boundary, and checks 122-127 exercise blocked and recovery states - no single successful send can produce a green.

rows.evidence_ref: Runtime probe of classify_integrity_severity at tested_commit: UNCLASSIFIED -> GREEN, SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE -> GREEN, SNAPSHOT_SKIPPED -> GREEN, BLOCKED_SEND_UNCLASSIFIED -> GREEN; only literal UNKNOWN -> RED. Core.py L1449-1451 sets UNCLASSIFIED when no hard-copy outcome applies.
rows.why: Executed proof of violation: UNCLASSIFIED, BLOCKED_SEND_UNCLASSIFIED and both stale-snapshot states hit the function's final 'return GREEN', so unclassified and unavailable classifications are published green instead of failing closed.

rows.evidence_ref: Probe classify_terminal_state(MASTER_REAL_ORDERS_OFF, MASTER_REAL_ORDERS_OFF, ENTRY, False) -> SEND_NOT_ATTEMPTED_AUTO_SEND_DISABLED; mapping Core.py L388-389; self-test 2-5 (intent written, zero send_attempt rows, no live_positions.json, no would_send_orders.csv)
rows.why: The disabled gate yields the explicit state SEND_NOT_ATTEMPTED_AUTO_SEND_DISABLED and checks 2-5 prove that in that state no send attempt and no live-position artefact is produced, so nothing can be claimed as live copy.

rows.evidence_ref: Probe: classify_integrity_severity(SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE) -> GREEN and (SNAPSHOT_SKIPPED) -> GREEN; fetch_snapshot L5668-5684 returns ({}, SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE); run_cycle L6491-6493; no entry gate consumes exchange_recon_status; self-test 1 shows SNAPSHOT_SKIPPED with leader_intents_written=1
rows.why: On a failed or skipped fresh exchange read the engine neither blocks the wallet/coin nor goes red - both states classify GREEN and entries continue writing intents - so the no-sizing / no-close / no-green requirement for a missing fresh exchange read is genuinely unmet.
